unit.title: Perform machining operations using horizontal and/or vertical boring machines

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main job of a boring machine?
options: To open up holes accurately to size and position
To cut sheet steel to shape with a long blade
To join two steel parts together with an electric arc
To bend flat plate into rings and curves

questions.stem: On a horizontal boring machine, which way does the spindle point?
options: Straight down at the table
Horizontally, across the table
Straight up from under the table
At a fixed 45° to the table

questions.stem: On a vertical boring mill, what turns while the metal is being cut?
options: Only the tool, held in a spindle
The column, round the fixed table
The work, clamped on a round table
The rail, from side to side

questions.stem: Which job is a horizontal boring machine best suited to?
options: Turning small pins from a short length of bar
Cutting threads on bolts in a die stock
Sharpening twist drills to the right angle
Boring in-line holes in a large gearbox case

questions.stem: Which job is a vertical boring mill best suited to?
options: Drilling small holes in thin sheet metal
Facing and boring a large, heavy round flange
Cutting angle iron to length for a frame
Bending plate into a curved shape

questions.stem: What is line boring?
options: Boring holes on one centre line in one set-up
Scribing a straight line on a plate for cutting
Boring a single hole at a set angle to the face
Drawing a line on the drawing through each hole

questions.stem: Why is a hole often bored after it is drilled, rather than only drilled?
options: Drilling alone is always much slower than boring
Boring leaves a rougher wall for oil to cling to
Boring corrects its position, size and finish
A drilled hole cannot be measured afterwards

questions.stem: What is a boring bar?
options: A steel bar used to lever heavy work into place
A long drill with two cutting lips at the end
A hardened bar used to check that a hole is round
A bar holding a cutting tool to cut inside a hole

questions.stem: What does an adjustable (offset) boring head let you do?
options: Change the spindle speed without stopping
Move the tool out in small steps to change the size
Clamp the work to the table more firmly
Measure the bore while the spindle turns

questions.stem: Why should a boring bar stick out of its holder no further than the job needs?
options: A long overhang bends and chatters
A short bar is easier to store away
A long bar makes the spindle run cold
A long bar uses up more cutting oil

questions.stem: A boring bar chatters and leaves a rough, wavy finish. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Raise the spindle speed as high as it goes
Switch off the coolant so the tool can grip
Shorten the overhang and check the clamping
Fit a longer and thinner boring bar

questions.stem: Why are carbide tool tips widely used for boring steel?
options: They are softer than steel, so cut more gently
They never need any coolant or chip control
They can be sharpened on a bench grinder
They hold an edge at higher cutting speeds

questions.stem: The spindle speed for boring is worked out as N = (Vc × 1000) ÷ (π × D). What does D stand for?
options: The depth of cut in mm
The bore diameter in mm
The length of the boring bar
The feed per turn in mm

questions.stem: A 100 mm bore is to be cut at a cutting speed of 25 m/min. Using N = (Vc × 1000) ÷ (π × D), about what spindle speed is needed?
options: 8 rpm
80 rpm
250 rpm
800 rpm

questions.stem: As the bore size gets larger, what should happen to the spindle speed for the same cutting speed?
options: It should go down
It should go up
It should stay the same
It should be doubled

questions.stem: What is the feed in a boring operation?
options: How fast the spindle turns each minute
How much coolant flows onto the tool
How far the tool moves along per turn
How deep the tool cuts into the wall

questions.stem: Why is a bore usually cut with roughing passes and then a light finishing pass?
options: So the bore does not need to be measured at the end
Because one heavy cut always breaks the machine
So that more different tools are used on each job
Rough cuts remove metal; a light cut gives size and finish

questions.stem: Where should clamps be placed when a casting is held on a boring machine table?
options: Close to the cut, over solid support
As far from the cut as the table allows
On a thin wall with no packing under it
Across the bore that is to be machined

questions.stem: Work is held down with a flat bar clamp, a bolt and a packing block. How should the packing block be set?
options: Well below the top face of the work
As far from the clamp bolt as it goes
Level with or just above the work face
Left out, so the bar sits on the table

questions.stem: Before an existing hole is bored, how is its centre found accurately on the machine?
options: By looking down the hole and judging by eye
By measuring from the edge with a tape
By trying cuts until the bore looks round
By clocking the bore with a dial indicator

questions.stem: Why is the work set square to the spindle and table before boring?
options: So the work looks neat for the photos
So the bore is true to the part's faces
So the cutting oil drains off the table
So the clamps are easier to fit on it

questions.stem: Which instrument can measure a 50 mm bore to 0.01 mm?
options: A steel rule held across the hole
A steel tape measure laid in it
An inside micrometer or bore gauge
The outside jaws of a caliper

questions.stem: How is a telescopic gauge used to measure a bore?
options: Lock it in the bore, then measure it with a micrometer
Read the size straight off the scale on its handle
Push it in and read the dial on the end
Tap it in with a soft hammer and read the gap

questions.stem: A bore is drawn as 40.00 mm +0.03/−0.00. Which measured size is acceptable?
When may a bore be measured during machining?
options: While the spindle is turning slowly
While the tool is still cutting
At any time, if you are careful
Only when the spindle has fully stopped

questions.stem: Why is cutting fluid used when boring steel?
options: To keep the floor round the machine clean
To give the bore a coat of protective paint
To cool the tool and help clear the chips
To make the tool chatter less on cast iron

questions.stem: Cast iron is usually bored dry. Why should a dust mask be worn?
options: Cast iron makes a fine black dust
The coolant gives off strong fumes
The machine is louder with cast iron
The bore reflects bright light

questions.stem: How should chips be cleared from a boring bar or the table?
options: By hand while the spindle is running slowly
With a brush or hook after the spindle stops
With compressed air blown towards your face
With a gloved hand while the tool is cutting

questions.stem: On a vertical boring mill, why must you never reach across the turning table?
options: It slows down the job and wastes the shift
Coolant may splash on your clothes and stain
The noise is louder over the table
The jaws and work can catch and drag you in

questions.stem: Delroy wants to wear cotton gloves while he operates the boring machine. What should he be told?
options: Gloves are fine as long as the speed is low
No gloves near turning parts, as they can be caught
Leather gloves are safe, but cotton are not
Two pairs are safer than one thin pair

questions.stem: At the Centre, who checks the set-up before the boring machine spindle is started?
options: The first trainee to arrive
Nobody, if the guards look fine
The assessor
The workshop cleaner

questions.stem: What must be removed from the machine before the spindle is started?
options: Spanners, keys and any loose tools
The clamps that are holding the work
The coolant pipe and its nozzle
The guard over the spindle nose

questions.stem: A gearbox casing weighs 300 kg. How should it be put on the boring machine table?
options: Lifted on by four strong people
Rolled up a plank onto the table
Lowered by a rope over a roof beam
With a crane and rated slings

questions.stem: What does a facing cut do on a boring machine?
options: Opens a small hole up to a bigger size
Cuts a screw thread inside the hole
Makes a flat surface square to the bore
Polishes the bore to a mirror finish

questions.stem: What is a counterbore?
options: A cone-shaped recess for a flat-head screw
A larger, flat-bottomed step at the mouth of a hole
A screw thread cut inside a hole with a tap
A long slot cut along the side of a bore

questions.stem: A bore measures 50.00 mm at the top and 50.08 mm at the bottom. What is this fault called?
options: Ovality
Chatter
Burr
Taper

questions.stem: Which is a common cause of a tapered bore?
options: The bar bending more as it goes deeper
Too much coolant on the top of the work
The colour of the boring bar's paint
Measuring the bore with a clean gauge

questions.stem: Before setting up, what must you read on the drawing for each bore?
options: Only the title block and the date drawn
Only the colour the part will be painted
Its size, tolerance, position and finish
Only the name of the person who drew it

questions.stem: Which change usually gives a smoother finish on the last boring pass?
options: A heavier cut and a coarser feed
Turning off the cutting fluid
Using a tool with a worn tip
A light cut and a finer feed

questions.stem: Which tool is held in the spindle to find the edge of the work and set a datum?
options: A reamer
An edge finder
A tap wrench
A centre punch

questions.stem: Before a boring head or bar is changed, what must be done?
options: Stop the spindle and isolate the machine
Slow the spindle down to its lowest speed
Let it run so the bar can be eased out
Open the guard and hold the bar by hand

questions.stem: After boring, why are the sharp edges at the ends of the bore removed?
options: So the part weighs less on the scales
So the bore takes paint more easily
They can cut hands and stop parts fitting
So the coolant drains out more quickly

questions.stem: At the end of the job, what should be done to the boring machine?
options: Leave it for the next shift to clean up
Hose it down with water to wash all the chips off
Take the guards off so it can dry out
Clean it, oil the slides, report any faults

questions.stem: A bore is 0.05 mm oversize after the finishing cut. What should the operator do?
options: Put it with the good parts and carry on
Stop, tag the part and tell the supervisor
Peen the bore with a hammer to close it up
Paint the bore so the size cannot be seen

questions.stem: What is the usual order of work when boring a hole in solid metal?
options: Centre drill, drill, rough bore, finish bore
Finish bore first, then rough bore, then drill
Rough bore, then centre drill, then drill
Ream to size, then drill, then rough bore

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go. Calculators are allowed if the Centre permits them.

shortAnswers.stem: A vertical boring mill looks like a large lathe standing on end. What is its other common name?
What is the name of the small cutting tip, clamped in a holder, that is turned to a fresh edge when it wears?
In the formula N = (Vc × 1000) ÷ (π × D), in what units is the cutting speed Vc usually given?
A 50 mm bore is cut at 31.4 m/min. Using N = (Vc × 1000) ÷ (π × D), what spindle speed, in rpm, is needed?
Which fluted tool is used to finish a drilled hole to an exact size and a smooth wall?
What is the name of the slotted groove in a machine table that holds clamping bolts?
A bore must be 80.00 mm +0.04/−0.00. What is the largest acceptable size, in mm?
What is the usual name for a clamp made of a flat bar with a bolt in the middle and a packing block at one end?
What is the name of the stepped steel block used to support the end of a clamp at the right height?
What is the name of the matched pair of accurate steel bars used to raise work evenly off the table?
What is the name of the short, stiff drill used first, to start a hole in the right place without wandering?
What is the name of the fault where a bore is not round but slightly oval?
What word describes the amount a size may vary from the drawing size and still be accepted?
Which lifting fitting, with a ring at the top, is screwed into a tapped hole in a casting so that it can be lifted?
Which part of a horizontal boring machine moves up and down the column, carrying the spindle?

essays.stem: Compare a horizontal boring machine with a vertical boring mill. Describe how each is laid out, what moves, and the kind of work each does best.
essays.modelAnswer: A horizontal boring machine has a spindle that points sideways. The spindle is carried in a headstock that moves up and down a column, and the work is clamped on a table that can move along and across, and often rotate. The spindle can slide out to bore deep holes, and a boring bar can be supported at both ends. It suits large, heavy, box-shaped parts such as gearbox casings, pump bodies and machine frames, where holes on one line must be bored in one set-up. A vertical boring mill is like a large lathe standing on end. The work is clamped on a big round table that turns, and the tools are carried on a rail above it and fed down or across. It suits large, heavy, round parts such as flanges, wheels, rings and pulleys, which are faced, turned and bored. On both machines the parts are too large or heavy for a normal lathe or mill.
markingPoints: Horizontal: sideways spindle in a headstock on a column; table moves (and rotates)
Horizontal: suits large box-shaped parts and in-line holes
Vertical: work turns on a large round table; tools on a rail feed down or across
Vertical: suits large round parts (flanges, wheels, rings)
Both handle parts too large for a normal lathe or mill

essays.stem: Describe how to set up a casting on the table of a horizontal boring machine ready for boring.
essays.modelAnswer: First read the drawing for the bore sizes, positions and datum faces, and check the casting for size and faults. Clean the table and the casting's base, and remove burrs. Lift the casting onto the table with a crane, rated slings or eyebolts, keeping hands clear of pinch points. Set it on parallels or packing so the tool can pass through without hitting the table, and so it does not rock. Clamp it close to where it will be cut, over solid support, with the packing blocks level with or just above the work face and the bolts near the work. Do not clamp across thin walls or the bore. Use a dial indicator to set the datum face square to the spindle and parallel to the table travel, tapping it into line before final tightening. Find the datum with an edge finder, or clock an existing hole to centre the spindle. The assessor checks the set-up before the spindle is started.
markingPoints: Reads the drawing; cleans table and work; removes burrs
Lifts with rated gear safely
Supports on parallels or packing; clamps near the cut over support, packing set correctly
Squares the datum face with a dial indicator
Finds the datum or centres on the bore; assessor checks before running

essays.stem: A 120 mm bore is to be cut with a carbide tool at a cutting speed of 90 m/min. Work out the spindle speed and explain how you would choose the speed actually set on the machine.
essays.modelAnswer: The formula is N = (Vc × 1000) ÷ (π × D), where N is the spindle speed in revolutions per minute, Vc is the cutting speed in metres per minute, and D is the bore diameter in millimetres. The 1000 changes metres into millimetres. So N = (90 × 1000) ÷ (3.142 × 120) = 90 000 ÷ 377 = about 239 rpm. If the machine has fixed speeds, I choose the nearest speed below this, for example 220 rpm, so the tool does not run too fast and burn. If it has variable speed, I set about 240 rpm. The cutting speed of 90 m/min itself should come from the tool maker's chart for that tool and material. I then watch and listen during the first cut: if the tool squeals, chatters or the chips turn blue, I reduce the speed; if the finish is good and the tool stays cool, the speed is right. The feed is set separately.
markingPoints: States the formula and what each letter means
Correct working: 90 000 ÷ (π × 120)
Answer about 239 rpm
Chooses the nearest lower available speed, or sets about 240 rpm
Cutting speed from the tool maker's chart; adjusts by watching the cut

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to bore a hole to size in solid metal on a boring machine.
essays.modelAnswer: First read the drawing for the size, tolerance and position of the hole, and set up and clamp the work square. Find the datum with an edge finder and move the spindle to the hole position. Have the assessor check the set-up. Start with a centre drill so the hole starts in the right place. Drill a pilot hole, then open it up with a larger drill, leaving a few millimetres for boring. Fit the boring bar or boring head with the shortest overhang that will reach. Set the speed and feed from the tool chart. Take roughing cuts to about 0.3–0.5 mm under size. Stop the spindle and measure the bore with an inside micrometer or a telescopic gauge and micrometer. Adjust the tool by the amount needed and take a light finishing cut at a finer feed. Stop and measure again, and repeat a very light cut if needed. Finally remove the sharp edges, clean the part and record the size.
markingPoints: Reads drawing; sets up, finds datum; set-up checked
Centre drills and drills, leaving metal for boring
Short overhang; correct speed and feed; roughing cuts leaving a finishing allowance
Stops the spindle to measure; adjusts; light finishing cut
Measures to tolerance, deburrs and records

essays.stem: Explain what causes chatter and a poor finish when boring, and describe how to cure them.
essays.modelAnswer: Chatter is a fast vibration of the tool against the work. It leaves a wavy, rough surface and a loud noise, and can chip the tool. The most common cause is a boring bar that sticks out too far, so it bends and springs. Other causes are a bar that is too thin for the hole, loose clamping or a loose tool, a blunt or chipped tool, too high a spindle speed, too light or too heavy a cut, and worn slides or bearings in the machine. To cure it, use the thickest bar that will fit and the shortest overhang that will reach. Tighten the clamps over solid support and check the tool is tight. Fit a sharp tool with the right shape. Lower the speed a little, or change the feed and depth of cut. A support at the far end of the bar helps on long bores. For a good finish, take a light last cut with a fine feed and use cutting fluid where the material needs it.
markingPoints: Describes chatter: vibration, wavy finish, noise
Long overhang or thin bar as main cause
Other causes: loose clamping, blunt tool, wrong speed, feed or cut
Cures: thick, short bar; tight clamping; sharp tool; adjust speed/feed
Light finishing cut with fine feed and suitable fluid

essays.stem: Describe how to measure a bore accurately, naming the instruments you could use and how each is used.
essays.modelAnswer: Always stop the spindle before measuring, clean the chips and fluid out of the bore, and let a hot part cool. A vernier caliper with its inside jaws gives a quick check to about 0.02 mm, but it is not accurate enough for a close tolerance. For accurate work, a telescopic gauge is put in the bore, rocked gently across it to find the largest size, locked, removed and then measured with an outside micrometer. An inside micrometer reads directly across the bore. A dial bore gauge is set to size with a ring gauge or micrometer and then rocked in the bore; it shows how far the bore is above or below the set size, and also shows taper and ovality. Measure at the top, middle and bottom of the bore and in two directions at right angles. Compare the readings with the size and tolerance on the drawing, and record them.
markingPoints: Stops the spindle, cleans the bore and lets it cool before measuring
Vernier caliper inside jaws for a quick check only
Telescopic gauge locked in the bore and measured with an outside micrometer
Inside micrometer or dial bore gauge (set to size; shows taper and ovality)
Measures at several depths and two directions; compares with tolerance; records

essays.stem: Describe the safety rules to follow when operating a horizontal or vertical boring machine.
essays.modelAnswer: Only use the machine after training and with permission. Wear safety glasses, safety boots and close-fitting overalls; roll up or button sleeves, remove rings and watches, and tie back long hair. Never wear gloves near the turning spindle, boring bar or table, because they can be caught. Keep all guards in place. Lift heavy work with a crane and rated slings, never by hand. Clamp the work securely, and remove spanners and keys before starting. The assessor checks the set-up before the spindle runs. Keep the table travel clear so the work cannot hit the column or a person. Never reach across a turning table or near a turning bar. Stop the spindle before measuring, adjusting the tool or clearing chips, and isolate the machine before changing tools or heads. Clear chips with a brush or hook, not by hand or with air towards anyone. Wear a dust mask when cutting cast iron, and avoid skin contact with cutting fluid.
markingPoints: Correct PPE and dress; no gloves near rotating parts
Guards on; work clamped; keys and spanners removed; assessor checks the set-up
Rated lifting gear for heavy work; table travel clear
Never reach across turning parts; stop to measure; isolate to change tools
Chips cleared with brush or hook; cast-iron dust and cutting-fluid precautions

essays.stem: Explain what line boring is, why it is needed for parts like gearbox casings, and how it is done on a horizontal boring machine.
essays.modelAnswer: Line boring means boring two or more holes, in different walls of a part, so that they share exactly the same centre line. A gearbox casing has bearing holes in its front and back walls. The shaft runs in bearings in both, so if the holes are not on one line, the shaft will bend, the bearings will run hot and wear out, and the gears will not mesh properly. On a horizontal boring machine the casing is set up square on the table and clamped. The spindle is lined up with the hole centre, and a long boring bar is passed through both walls. On long jobs the far end of the bar is held in an outer support. Both holes are rough bored and then finish bored without moving the work, so they stay in line. Each hole is measured, and the alignment can be checked with a test bar that must pass freely through both holes.
markingPoints: Definition: holes in separate walls bored on one centre line
Why: shafts and bearings need true alignment; otherwise wear, heat, poor gear mesh
Work set square and clamped; spindle lined up with the centre
Long bar through both walls, supported; bored without moving the work
Measured and checked with a test bar

essays.stem: Describe how to care for a boring machine and its tools at the end of a job.
essays.modelAnswer: First stop the machine and isolate it as the Centre's rules require. Remove the work with the right lifting gear and put it in the right place, labelled. Take out the boring bar, head and tools, clean them, and check the cutting tips for wear or chips; replace or report damaged ones and store them in their holders, not loose in a drawer. Clear the chips from the table, T-slots and slides with a brush and chip hook, and put them in the chip bin; keep steel and cast iron apart if the Centre recycles them. Wipe off cutting fluid. Oil the slides and other points the maker's chart shows, and check the fluid and oil levels. Put clamps, step blocks and parallels back in their racks. Wipe and store measuring instruments in their cases. Report any faults, such as noises, leaks or damaged guards, to the instructor, and fill in the machine log. Sweep the floor so no one slips.
markingPoints: Stops and isolates; removes the work safely
Cleans, checks and stores tools; reports worn tips
Clears chips from table and slides with brush/hook; wipes fluid
Lubricates as the maker says; returns clamps and instruments
Reports faults, fills in the log, leaves the floor safe

essays.stem: Explain how an adjustable boring head is used to bring a bore to its final size, and why the last cut is kept light.
essays.modelAnswer: An adjustable boring head fits in the spindle and holds a small boring bar on a slide that can be moved out from the centre by a fine screw with a graduated dial. Moving the tool out makes the bore larger. After the roughing cuts, the spindle is stopped and the bore is measured. The difference between this size and the size wanted is worked out. Because the tool cuts on both sides of the hole, the tool is moved out by half this amount. For example, if the bore is 31.80 mm and 32.00 mm is wanted, the diameter must grow by 0.20 mm, so the tool is moved out by 0.10 mm; the dial on some heads already reads in diameter, so the maker's markings must be checked. The slide is locked, and a light finishing cut is taken at a fine feed. The last cut is kept light because a light cut bends the bar less, so the size is more exact and the finish is smoother.
markingPoints: Head holds the tool on a slide moved out by a graduated screw
Measures after roughing and works out the difference
Moves the tool by half the diameter change (or checks if the dial reads diameter)
Correct example (0.20 mm on diameter = 0.10 mm tool move)
Light final cut bends the bar less: exact size and smoother finish

practical1.title: Drill and bore a hole to size in a steel or aluminium block
practical1.brief: As a group, bore a 32.00 mm hole (+0.05 / −0.00) through the centre of a 100 mm × 100 mm × 40 mm block of mild steel or aluminium. Use the Centre's horizontal or vertical boring machine. If the Centre has no boring machine, use a vertical milling machine with an adjustable boring head, and say so on the record. Read the drawing and plan the steps on the job sheet. Clamp the block on parallels, square it, and find its centre with an edge finder. The assessor checks the set-up before the spindle is started. Centre drill, drill and open the hole up, leaving metal for boring. Work out the spindle speed from the cutting speed the instructor gives, rough bore, stop and measure, adjust the boring head and finish bore to size. Remove the sharp edges and measure the bore at the top, middle and bottom. Each member takes one cut or adjustment and takes one set of measurements while the others watch the machine. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Mild steel or aluminium block, 100 mm × 100 mm × 40 mm, faces square
Horizontal or vertical boring machine; or a vertical milling machine with an adjustable boring head
Clamps, T-bolts, step blocks and parallels
Edge finder, centre drill and twist drills
Boring head or boring bar with sharp tools
Telescopic gauges and outside micrometer, or inside micrometer; vernier caliper
Cutting fluid, brush and chip hook, deburring tool
photos: The job sheet with the planned steps and the speed worked out
The block clamped on parallels and squared
The edge finder setting the datum, and the assessor's set-up check
The hole drilled and the boring bar set in it
The bore being measured with the spindle stopped
The finished bore with its measurements recorded, and the cleaned machine
checklist: Planned the steps and worked out the spindle speed correctly
Clamped the work over support and set it square
Found the centre with an edge finder
Took a boring cut with the right speed, feed and short overhang
Stopped the spindle before measuring and adjusting
Measured the bore correctly and adjusted the tool by the right amount
Finished within tolerance (32.00 to 32.05 mm) and removed sharp edges
Wore the right PPE, no gloves near turning parts, and cleaned the machine
safety: Guards on; the assessor checks the set-up before the spindle runs
No gloves, rings or loose sleeves near the turning spindle; tie back long hair
Stop the spindle before measuring, adjusting or clearing chips; use a brush or chip hook
Remove spanners and keys before starting; wear safety glasses and safety boots

practical2.title: Line bore the two lugs of a fabricated bracket for a shaft
practical2.brief: As a group, line bore a 25.00 mm hole (+0.05 / −0.00) through both lugs of a fabricated steel bracket, so that a 25 mm test bar slides through both holes. The bracket is a base plate with two parallel lugs about 100 mm apart, welded on earlier or supplied by the instructor. Read the drawing and plan the job. Set the bracket on the horizontal boring machine table, square the lugs to the spindle with a dial indicator, and clamp it near the lugs over solid support. If the Centre has no horizontal boring machine, set the bracket on its side on a vertical milling machine so that the hole axis is vertical, and bore both lugs from one set-up without moving the work; say so on the record. The assessor checks the set-up before the spindle runs. Find the hole centre from the datum, centre drill and drill through both lugs, then bore both to size without moving the work. Stop and measure each hole, then try the test bar through both. Each member takes part in setting up, takes one cut, and measures one hole. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Fabricated steel bracket with two parallel lugs about 10–12 mm thick and 100 mm apart
Horizontal boring machine; or a vertical milling machine with a long-reach boring bar or boring head
Clamps, step blocks, parallels and angle plate
Dial indicator with magnetic base, edge finder
Centre drill, twist drills, boring bar with sharp tool
Telescopic gauges and outside micrometer, or inside micrometer
Cutting fluid, brush, chip hook and deburring tool
photos: The bracket and drawing, with the hole centre and datum marked
The bracket clamped and the lugs being squared with a dial indicator
The assessor's set-up check, with keys and spanners removed
Drilling through both lugs from one set-up
Each bore being measured with the spindle stopped
The test bar passing through both lugs, and the cleaned machine
checklist: Read the drawing and found the hole centre from the datum
Set the lugs square to the spindle with a dial indicator
Clamped over support near the lugs without distorting them
Drilled and bored both lugs without moving the work
Stopped the spindle to measure and adjust
Both holes within tolerance and the test bar slides through both
Removed sharp edges and recorded the sizes
Worked safely with no gloves near turning parts, and cleaned up
safety: Guards on; the assessor checks the set-up before the spindle runs
No gloves near the turning spindle or bar; gloves only when handling sharp-edged plate with the machine stopped
Keep the table travel clear and never reach across turning parts
Stop the spindle before measuring; clear chips with a brush or hook; wear safety glasses and boots
